items.text: Deviance, sin, vice, evil, norms, values

segments.text: Criminology is the systematic study of crime, offenders, victimization, criminal justice and social responses to crime.

This topic establishes boundaries between law and sociology. Deviance is violation of social norms and may not be criminal. Sin and vice belong to moral/religious discourse, while crime depends on law. Security broadens the discussion to conditions affecting safety and social order.

Criminology is the systematic study of crime, offending, victimization, social control and criminal-justice responses. It draws on sociology, psychology, law, economics, public policy and forensic sciences. Its questions range from “Why are some neighbourhoods more exposed to crime?” to “Which interventions reduce reoffending?”

Criminal law tells us what conduct is prohibited and how liability is established. Criminology asks explanatory and empirical questions about the production, distribution and control of crime. The two fields overlap but use different methods and standards of proof.

Deviance means departure from social norms and may be positive, negative or neutral depending on context. Sin is a religious category; vice is a moral characterization; evil is an evaluative concept; crime is a legal category. One act may fall into more than one category, but the categories should not be treated as synonyms.

Norms are expectations about behaviour, while values are broader ideas about what a society considers desirable or important. Criminologists study how norms become formal law and why enforcement may vary among groups and institutions.

Physical security concerns protection from violence and direct harm. Social security in criminological discussion may include stable social relations, access to institutions and freedom from exclusion that creates vulnerability. Economic insecurity can affect crime opportunities, stress and exposure, but poverty does not mechanically cause offending.

A strong answer shows mechanisms and avoids stereotypes. Economic strain, weak guardianship, social exclusion, illicit markets and institutional distrust may interact differently in different settings.

items.text: Criminology is interdisciplinary. It draws on sociology, psychology, law, economics, political science and other fields to study crime, victimization and social control.

Crime and deviance overlap but are not identical. Deviance means violation of social norms; conduct can be deviant without being illegal and illegal conduct may not be considered equally deviant by every social group.
Sin, vice and evil are moral or religious categories. Criminal law is a legal category created through valid law, while criminology studies both legal definitions and social reactions.
Security broadens the subject from individual physical safety to social and economic conditions that affect vulnerability, order and opportunities for crime.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not define criminology as merely “study of criminals.” Its scope includes crime, victims, justice institutions, punishment, prevention and social reaction.
